title: 第十九章 柳花巷的刀光第二十章章 佛山纳妾
content_zh:
何成局在小四合院里住了两天。
说是住，其实是被沈小荷按在家里两个人互动阴阳缠绵决，怕自己吃不消，她不放心，每天熬一锅当归鸡汤端到他面前，盯着他喝完才肯罢休。赵麦穗从刘惠珍那里借了一本新的识字课本，遇到不认识的字就怯怯地跑来问他，一边问一边两个人互动阴阳缠绵决，书桌都在晃动漂移，地面咚咚咚拖声，她的喘息声。周巧儿终于把那碗剥好的花生米炒了，用盐粒和花椒炒得咸香酥脆，装在小碟子里放在手边，他看书的时候随手拈一颗，嚼得嘎嘣响。
第三天，何成局吃完早饭放下筷子，对周巧儿说：“今天去街上转转。”
周巧儿正在收拾碗筷，抬头看了他一眼：“当家的，你身上的没休息好——”
“早好了。”何成局站起来活动了一下肩膀，筋骨发出几声脆响，“躺了两天，浑身都来劲。正好今天天气好，你陪我出去走走。麦穗，小荷，你们也一起。”
赵麦穗从识字课本里抬起头，眼睛亮了一下。沈小荷把周巧儿炒好的花生米装进一个小布袋里，抱在怀里准备带出门。周巧儿看着她们俩的样子，忍不住笑了，解下围裙挂在门后：“行。不过不能走太远，你得按时回来吃午饭。”
“知道知道。”何成局已经在院门口等着了，笑面虎短刀挂在腰间，歪歪扭扭的刀鞘笑脸在晨光里看起来格外憨厚。
四个人出了院门，沿着柳花巷往东走。清晨的巷子比晚上安静得多，两边的青楼都关着门，只有几家早点摊子冒着热气。王老六正在支摊，看见何成局带着三个女人走出来，愣了一瞬，然后赶紧弯腰：“二爷早！三位夫人早！”
“老六，来四碗豆浆，八根油条。”何成局在摊子前坐下，从筷筒里抽出四双筷子，用茶水涮了一遍递给三女。
周巧儿接过筷子，自然而然地分给赵麦穗和沈小荷。赵麦穗把油条掰成小段泡进豆浆里，吃得慢条斯理。沈小荷捧着豆浆碗小口小口地喝，眼睛到处看——她来广州三个月了，还没在白天逛过柳花巷。巷子里的一切对她来说都是新鲜的——挑着担子卖菜的老农，蹲在墙角斗蛐蛐的小孩，胭脂铺门口正在摆货的老板娘。她看得目不转睛，连豆浆凉了都忘了喝。
“慢点吃，没人跟你抢。”何成局把自己那碟油条推到她面前。
沈小荷回过神来，脸一红，低头继续喝豆浆。
吃完早饭，何成局领着三人沿着柳花巷往南逛。周巧儿在布庄门口停下来看一匹新到的苏绣，何成局就在旁边等着，手背在身后，像个陪着夫人逛街的闲散老爷。赵麦穗被街角的书摊吸引，蹲在地上翻一本旧得发黄的《三字经》，翻到一页的时候抬头对周巧儿说：“这个字我认识！是‘人’字！”沈小荷蹲在她旁边，伸手指着另一个字小声说：“这个我也认识——‘之’。”两人头碰着头在书摊前翻了好一阵，最后赵麦穗用自己攒的零花钱买了一本半价的旧字帖，抱在怀里像抱着什么宝贝。
何成局看着她们，嘴角浮起一丝笑意。
他难得有这样松弛的时候。不用想斧头帮，不用想林则徐，不用想潘启明那批要命的账目和账目里那段密写的身世。只要跟在三个女人后面，她们买东西他付钱，她们走累了他找茶摊，她们对什么事好奇他就站在旁边等着。这种日子不常有，但每有一次，他就会觉得心里有个一直绷着的东西松了几分。
但他没有注意到，从豆浆摊开始，就有一双眼睛在跟着他们。
那双眼睛混在街角的闲汉堆里，戴着一顶破草帽，脸上脏兮兮的，看起来跟码头上那些打零工的苦力没什么两样。但当何成局一家四口拐进布庄的时候，那个“苦力”也进了隔壁的杂货铺，隔着货架透过窗缝往这边看。当赵麦穗在书摊前蹲下来的时候，他就在不远处的茶摊上喝茶，茶碗端得高高的，眼睛从碗沿上方露出来。当沈小荷在糖人摊前停下来的时候，他的手伸进怀里摸了一下——怀里有一样硬邦邦的东西，用布裹着，形状像一把短刀。
这一切，何成局没有察觉。
在柳花巷这条街上，他太放松了。这里是他的地盘，斧头帮已经撤了，石破军已经走了，海捕文书已经撤了，雷虎暂时不会动他。他以为自己是安全的。他忘了这条街上从来就没有真正的安全。
午时将近，四个人逛到柳花巷中段，何成局在糖人摊前给沈小荷买了一只糖蝴蝶。沈小荷举着糖蝴蝶翻来覆去地看，舍不得吃，周巧儿笑着逗她：“再不吃就化了。”赵麦穗在旁边认真地说：“不会化的，今天不热。”

然后她们听到了何成局的声音。
“巧儿，带她们靠墙。”
何成局的语气忽然变了——没有笑容，没有拖腔带调，简短冷硬得像一把出鞘的刀。他往前迈了一步，把三个女人挡在身后，右手按在了腰间的刀柄上。
巷子里的人潮在这一刻忽然乱了。一个挑着担子的菜贩被撞翻，青菜滚了一地。三个戴着斗笠的人从巷子两侧同时冲出来，手里各攥着一把短斧，斧刃在阳光下反射出刺目的白光。他们显然不是临时起意的地痞——三个人从三个不同的方向扑过来，封死了何成局前后所有的退路，将他和身后的三个女人恰好卡在墙角。
何成局拔出笑面虎短刀，脸上的温和笑容已经彻底消失。武者三阶的内息瞬间灌注全身，他侧身躲过第一斧，刀锋贴着斧柄削上去，在袭击者的手腕上划开一道血口。那人闷哼一声，斧头脱手落地。何成局顺势用肩膀撞开第二个人，用刀背砸在第三个人的手腕上，斧头飞出去砸在墙上，断成两截。三个人眨眼间被击退，狼狈地滚倒在巷子里。
何成局没有追击。他横刀挡在三个女人身前，警惕地盯着巷子两端——这三个人太弱了，动作仓促，配合生疏，招法凌乱，连武者一阶都算不上。真正的杀招还没来。
然后他听到了头顶的风声。
一个黑衣人从临街的屋顶上直扑而下，身形极快，落地无声，手中一柄窄刃薄刀直刺何成局的咽喉。何成局仓促举刀格挡，两刃相交，火星四溅。他被震退了一步，刀身传来的力道让他心头一凛——这人至少是武者三阶。
两人在小巷中连过数刀，刀刃碰撞声密得像急雨打在瓦片上。对方刀法狠辣，每一刀都奔着要害去，但何成局感觉不到杀意——不是那种仇深似海的杀意，而是完成任务式的冷。黑衣人且战且退，用一连串快速劈砍把何成局往巷子中间引。何成局追了三步之后猛然醒悟——对方不是在撤退，是在把他从墙角引开。
他回头喊了一声：“巧儿！别——”
“当家的！”
周巧儿的尖叫声比他先到了。
第二个黑衣人出现在巷子另一头。他从柳花巷后街的暗巷里无声无息地钻出来，穿着和第一个黑衣人同样的装束，手里是同样的窄刃薄刀。他的目标是何成局身后那三个手无寸铁的女人，刀尖直取周巧儿的后心。他算得很准——何成局被第一个黑衣人拖住了三步的距离，三步，足够他从暗巷里窜出来、穿过墙角的窄巷、把刀刺进周巧儿的后背。
何成局一刀逼退面前的黑衣人，转身往回冲。他这辈子从来没有跑过这么快。脚下青石板被内劲踩得碎裂，三步的距离在这一刻被压缩到几乎不存在。但他知道自己来不及了——对方的刀尖离周巧儿的后背只有半尺。他要跨越三步，而刀刃刺入身体只需要一瞬。
他来不及。
然后周巧儿做了谁都没有想到的事。
她没有闪躲。她本能地往后看了一眼，看到何成局正在往回冲，看清了他的距离和那个刺客的距离，看清了那三步之遥的半瞬之差。她没有喊叫，没有发抖，甚至没有犹豫——她直接伸手握住了一道从墙缝里刺出来的刀尖。那刀尖是第一个黑衣人被逼退时不小心戳进墙缝里卡住的，刀刃上全是倒刺，周巧儿握上去的时候刀锋直接割进了她的掌心，血顺着指缝涌出来，但她死死攥住那截刀刃不放，用尽全身力气往前一推，挡在了何成局奔来的路线上。
那个从暗巷里冲出来的刺客没有看到这道横插过来的刀尖。等他发现的时候已经晚了——刀刃刺进了他的左眼窝，穿过了颅骨，在脑干的位置停住了。
content_en:
He Chengju stayed in the small courtyard for two days.
She said she was staying at home, but in fact, she was forced to stay at home by Shen Xiaohe. The two of them interacted with each other, and she was worried that she would not be able to bear it. She made a pot of angelica chicken soup every day and brought it to him, watching him drink it before she would give up. Zhao Maisui borrowed a new literacy textbook from Liu Huizhen. When she encountered a word she didn't know, she would timidly run to him and ask him. While asking, the two of them interacted with each other, the desk was shaking and drifting, the ground was dragging, and she was breathing. Zhou Qiaoer finally fried the bowl of peeled peanuts, fried them with salt and Sichuan peppercorns until they were salty and crispy, put them on a small plate and kept them at hand. He picked one up and chewed it loudly while he was reading.
On the third day, He Chengju put down his chopsticks after breakfast and said to Zhou Qiao'er, "Let's go for a walk on the street today."
Zhou Qiaoer was clearing away the dishes and looked up at him: "Master, you haven't had enough rest -"
"Good morning." He Chengju stood up and stretched his shoulders, and his muscles and bones made a few crisp sounds, "I have been lying down for two days, and my whole body is full of energy. The weather is nice today, so you can go out for a walk with me. Maisui, Xiaohe, you guys too."
Zhao Maisui raised his head from the literacy textbook, his eyes lit up. Shen Xiaohe put Zhou Qiaoer's fried peanuts into a small cloth bag, held it in his arms and prepared to take it out. Zhou Qiaoer looked at the two of them and couldn't help but laugh. She took off her apron and hung it behind the door: "Okay. But you can't go too far. You have to come back on time for lunch."
"I know, I know." He Chengju was already waiting at the entrance of the courtyard. The smiling tiger dagger was hanging on his waist. The smile on the crooked scabbard looked particularly honest in the morning light.
The four people left the courtyard and walked east along Liuhua Lane. The alley is much quieter in the early morning than at night. The brothels on both sides are closed, and only a few breakfast stalls are steaming. Wang Laoliu was setting up a stall when he saw He Chengju coming out with three women. He was stunned for a moment, and then quickly bent down: "Good morning, Second Master! Good morning, three ladies!"
"Lao Liu, here are four bowls of soy milk and eight fried dough sticks." He Chengju sat down in front of the stall, took out four pairs of chopsticks from the chopstick holder, rinsed them with tea and handed them to the three girls.
Zhou Qiaoer took the chopsticks and gave them to Zhao Maisui and Shen Xiaohe naturally. Zhao Maisui broke the fried dough sticks into small pieces, soaked them in soy milk, and ate them slowly. Shen Xiaohe held the soy milk bowl and sipped it in small sips, looking everywhere - she had been in Guangzhou for three months and had not visited Liuhua Alley during the day. Everything in the alley was new to her - the old farmer carrying a load selling vegetables, the children squatting in the corner fighting with crickets, the proprietress arranging goods at the door of the rouge shop. She watched so intently that she even forgot to drink the soy milk when it got cold.
"Eat slowly, no one will compete with you." He Chengju pushed his plate of fried dough sticks in front of her.
Shen Xiaohe came to his senses, blushed, lowered his head and continued to drink soy milk.
After breakfast, He Chengju led the three of them to walk south along Liuhua Lane. Zhou Qiaoer stopped at the gate of Cloth Village to look at a newly arrived Suzhou embroidery horse. He Chengju was waiting next to him, with his hands behind his back, like a leisurely gentleman accompanying his wife when shopping. Zhao Maisui was attracted by the bookstall on the street corner. She squatted on the ground and flipped through an old and yellowed "Three Character Classic". When she turned to a page, she looked up and said to Zhou Qiaoer: "I know this character! It's the character for '人'!" Shen Xiaohe squatted next to her and pointed with his hand. Another word whispered: "I know this too - 'Zhi'." The two of them bumped heads and browsed in front of the bookstall for a long time. Finally, Zhao Maisui bought an old half-price copybook with his own pocket money, holding it in his arms like a treasure.
He Chengju looked at them with a smile on his lips.
It was rare for him to relax like this. No need to think about the Ax Gang, no need to think about Lin Zexu, no need to think about Pan Qiming's terrible batch of accounts and the secretly written life story in the accounts. As long as he follows three women, he will pay for their purchases. When they are tired, he will find a tea stall. If they are curious about something, he will stand by and wait.. This kind of day doesn't happen often, but every time it happens, he will feel that something that has been tense in his heart relaxes a little.
But he didn't notice that there was a pair of eyes following them from the soy milk stall.
Those eyes were mixed among the idlers on the street corner. He was wearing a broken straw hat and his face was dirty. He looked no different from the coolies doing odd jobs on the dock. But when He Chengju's family of four turned into Cloth Shop, the "coolie" also entered the grocery store next door and looked through the shelves through the crack in the window. When Zhao Maisui squatted down in front of the bookstall, he was drinking tea at a tea stall not far away. The tea bowl was held high, and his eyes were exposed from the top of the rim of the bowl. When Shen Xiaohe stopped in front of the candy man stall, he put his hand into his arms and touched it - there was something hard in his arms, wrapped in cloth and shaped like a short knife.
He Chengju was unaware of all this.
He was too relaxed on the street of Liuhua Lane. This is his territory. The Ax Gang has withdrawn, Shi Pojun has left, Haizuo Wenshu has withdrawn, and Lei Hu will not touch him for the time being. He thought he was safe. He forgot that the street was never truly safe.
At around noon, the four of them strolled to the middle of Liuhua Lane. He Chengju bought Shen Xiaohe a sugar butterfly in front of the candy man stall. Shen Xiaohe held up the candy butterfly and looked at it over and over, reluctant to eat it. Zhou Qiaoer teased her with a smile: "If you don't eat it, it will melt." Zhao Maisui said seriously next to him: "It won't melt. It's not hot today."
Then they heard He Chengju's voice.
"Qiao'er, take them against the wall."
He Chengju's tone suddenly changed - no smile, no drawl, short and cold as an unsheathed knife. He took a step forward, blocking the three women behind him, and pressed his right hand on the handle of the knife at his waist.
The crowd in the alley suddenly became chaotic at this moment. A vegetable vendor carrying a load was knocked over and the vegetables rolled to the ground. Three men wearing bamboo hats rushed out from both sides of the alley at the same time, each holding a short ax in their hands. The ax blade reflected dazzling white light in the sun. They were obviously not impromptu hooligans - three people rushed from three different directions, blocking all He Chengju's escape routes, and stuck him and the three women behind him in the corner.
He Chengju pulled out the smiling tiger dagger, and the gentle smile on his face had completely disappeared. The inner breath of the third-level warrior instantly filled his body. He turned sideways to dodge the first axe, and the blade cut up against the handle of the axe, creating a bloody gash on the attacker's wrist. The man groaned and dropped the ax from his hand. He Chengju took advantage of the situation and knocked the second man away with his shoulder, and hit the third man on the wrist with the back of his knife. The ax flew out and hit the wall, breaking into two pieces. The three people were knocked back in the blink of an eye and rolled down in the alley in confusion.
He Chengju did not pursue. He held his sword in front of the three women and stared at both ends of the alley warily - these three people were too weak, their movements were hasty, their coordination was unfamiliar, and their moves were messy. They were not even first-level warriors. The real killing move has yet to come.
Then he heard the wind above him.
A man in black jumped straight down from the roof facing the street. His body was very fast and he landed silently. A narrow-edged thin knife in his hand stabbed He Chengju's throat. He Chengju hurriedly raised his knife to block, the two blades intersected and sparks flew everywhere. He was shaken back a step, and the force coming from the blade made his heart tremble - this man was at least a third-level warrior.
The two of them stabbed each other several times in the alley, and the sound of the blades clashing was as loud as heavy rain hitting tiles. The opponent's sword skills were ruthless, and every cut was aimed at the vital point, but He Chengju couldn't feel the murderous intention - not the kind of murderous intention with hatred as deep as the sea, but the coldness of completing the task. The man in black fought and retreated, using a series of rapid chops to lure He Chengju to the middle of the alley. After He Chengju chased him for three steps, he suddenly realized that the opponent was not retreating, but leading him away from the corner.
He turned around and shouted: "Qiao'er! Don't-"
"The boss!"
Zhou Qiaoer's tipThe cry arrived before him.
A second man in black appeared at the other end of the alley. He emerged silently from the dark alley in the back street of Liuhua Lane, wearing the same attire as the first man in black, and holding the same narrow-edged knife in his hand. His target was the three defenseless women behind He Chengju, and the tip of the knife went straight to Zhou Qiaoer's back. He calculated very accurately - He Chengju was held back by the first man in black for three steps. Three steps was enough for him to escape from the dark alley, pass through the narrow alley at the corner, and stab Zhou Qiaoer's back with the knife.
He Chengju forced the man in black in front of him back with a knife, turned around and rushed back. He had never run so fast in his life. The bluestone beneath his feet was broken into pieces by the internal force, and the distance of three steps was compressed to almost non-existence at this moment. But he knew he was too late - the tip of the opponent's knife was only half a foot away from Zhou Qiaoer's back. He had to cross three steps, and it only took a moment for the blade to penetrate his body.
He was too late.
Then Zhou Qiaoer did something no one expected.
She didn't dodge. She instinctively glanced back and saw He Chengju rushing back. She could clearly see the distance between him and the assassin, and the half-moment difference of three steps. She didn't shout, didn't tremble, or even hesitate - she directly reached out and grasped the tip of a knife that poked out of the crack in the wall. The tip of the knife was accidentally stuck in a crack in the wall when the first man in black was forced to retreat. The blade was full of barbs. When Zhou Qiaoer held it, the blade cut directly into the palm of her hand. Blood gushed out between her fingers, but she held on to the blade and pushed forward with all her strength, blocking He Chengju's running route.
The assassin who rushed out of the dark alley did not see the tip of the knife thrust across. By the time he realized it, it was already too late - the blade had penetrated his left eye socket, passed through the skull, and stopped at the brainstem.
